question: What is the main goal of an OSCE in midwifery training?
explanation: An OSCE is designed to test hands-on clinical performance rather than theoretical knowledge alone. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T10#BMP312_U3_T10_h1)

question: Why is the OSCE considered a fair and objective method of assessment?

options.A: Students choose their own clinical tasks
options.B: Examiners grade based on personal impression
options.C: Questions change depending on student ability
options.D: Every student is marked using identical criteria

explanation: Objectivity means removing personal bias by using standardized checklists so all candidates are judged by the same standard. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T10#BMP312_U3_T10_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a goal of using OSCEs in training?
explanation: OSCEs complement clinical placements rather than replace them, serving as a safe bridge to real patient care. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T10#BMP312_U3_T10_h2)

question: A student passes her written paper on postpartum hemorrhage but struggles to manage simulated bleeding during an OSCE. What does this show?

options.A: That the student does not need any remediation
options.B: That practical exams are completely unnecessary
options.C: A gap between theoretical knowledge and practical execution
options.D: An error in the written grading system

explanation: Writing about a procedure is very different from performing it under pressure, which is exactly what OSCEs are built to uncover. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T10#BMP312_U3_T10_h2)

question: What happens at an interactive OSCE station?

options.A: The student takes a mandatory tea break
options.B: The student repairs an actual human tear without supervision
options.C: The student engages with a standardized patient or actor
options.D: The student sits quietly and answers multiple-choice items

explanation: Interactive stations specifically test communication, counseling, and history-taking skills using simulated patients. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T10#BMP312_U3_T10_h3)

question: Why are rest stations sometimes included in an OSCE circuit?

options.A: To allow examiners time to change the grading rubric
options.B: To give students a brief mental break and prevent fatigue
options.C: To replace active stations when equipment breaks down
options.D: To punish students who finish their tasks too quickly

explanation: Moving rapidly through high-pressure stations is mentally draining, so rest spots help maintain fair performance levels. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T10#BMP312_U3_T10_h3)

question: What kind of clinical scenarios should educators focus on for OSCE stations?

options.C: Abstract medical theories with no practical use
options.D: Complex surgical procedures meant for consultants

explanation: Midwifery students should be tested on real situations they will encounter frequently in routine and emergency maternity care. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T10#BMP312_U3_T10_h4)

question: What is the main problem with using unclear instructions at an OSCE station door?

options.A: It makes the examination take twice as long
options.B: It prevents the use of standardized patients
options.C: It causes student panic and unfair grading
options.D: It forces examiners to grade without checklists

explanation: Unclear prompts test guessing ability rather than actual clinical competence, compromising the validity of the exam. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T10#BMP312_U3_T10_h4)

question: What is the main function of an objective checklist in an OSCE?

options.A: To score specific, step-by-step procedural actions
options.B: To replace the need for an examiner inside the room
options.C: To calculate the final grade point average of the school
options.D: To judge the student's personal mood during the exam

explanation: Checklists break down a procedure into discrete actions so examiners can mark presence or absence objectively. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T10#BMP312_U3_T10_h5)

question: A student completes every procedural step on a checklist for an injection but is rough and ignores the patient. Which tool will most likely catch this issue?
explanation: Global rating scales assess holistic qualities like demeanor, confidence, and patient rapport that rigid checklists might miss. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T10#BMP312_U3_T10_h5)

question: How should an examiner generally behave during an active OSCE station?

options.A: Chat warmly with the student to reduce examination anxiety
options.B: Leave the room and grade based on the finished product
options.C: Remain a silent, neutral observer with a blank expression
options.D: Actively guide the student step-by-step through the task

explanation: Examiners must not give verbal or non-verbal cues that could unfairly influence the student's performance or score. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T10#BMP312_U3_T10_h6)

question: Why are faculty calibration sessions important before holding an OSCE?

options.A: To ensure all examiners interpret the grading rubric the same way
options.B: To decide which students will pass or fail beforehand
options.C: To change the examination questions based on student gossip
options.D: To give teachers a chance to relax before grading begins

explanation: Calibration prevents different examiners from grading too harshly or too leniently, keeping scoring fair and reliable. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T10#BMP312_U3_T10_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of holding a mock OSCE before the real exam?

options.A: To save money on clinical training equipment
options.B: To permanently replace final board certification exams
options.C: To remove the fear of the unknown through practice
options.D: To test how many students can fail in one afternoon

explanation: Mock exams familiarize students with the physical layout, timing, and pressure of the actual OSCE environment. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T10#BMP312_U3_T10_h7)

question: How does reviewing sample checklists with peers help a midwifery student prepare?

options.A: It teaches her to view procedures from the examiner's perspective
options.B: It ensures she never has to take the actual exam
options.C: It allows her to award herself a passing grade early
options.D: It eliminates the need for faculty supervision entirely

explanation: Grading peers helps students understand what critical steps examiners look for, improving their own clinical mindfulness. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T10#BMP312_U3_T10_h7)

question: Which of the following is a common challenge when running OSCEs in large schools?

options.A: An excess of highly functional electronic equipment
options.B: Too many examiners available for every single station
options.C: Unlimited electricity and reliable power supply
options.D: Limited simulation manikins and space constraints

explanation: Many schools struggle with shortages of proper anatomical models and adequate testing rooms for large classes. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T10#BMP312_U3_T10_h8)

question: An unexpected power outage occurs right in the middle of a midday OSCE circuit. What is the most practical backup plan?

options.A: Guess the final scores based on past semester records
options.B: Switch immediately to manual bells and paper checklists
options.C: Wait hours for the electricity grid to restore power
options.D: Cancel the entire examination and send all students home

explanation: Having low-tech backups like manual timers and paper sheets ensures the exam can continue smoothly despite infrastructure failures. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T10#BMP312_U3_T10_h8)
